tourism.detail: Australia is on the eligible-country list. The eVisa is normally one-year multiple entry with a maximum stay of three months and is not extendable.
tourism.next: Apply on the official Visit Saudi portal, carry the issued eVisa and respect its tourism-only purpose.
tourism.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

meetings.detail: A Saudi entity requests the commercial visit and documents the purpose. Ordinary business-visit activity does not authorise employment or contracted delivery.
meetings.next: Have the Saudi company issue the invitation and keep the schedule to negotiations, partner meetings and site visits.
meetings.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

conference.route: Event visit or commercial visit arranged for attendance and participation
conference.detail: Saudi Arabia's visa platform includes an event-visit request for attendance or participation. The organiser must still confirm access and visa support; registration is not permission to speak or work.
conference.next: Ask the organiser which event or commercial invitation it will issue and whether delegate accreditation is restricted.
conference.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

unpaid-speaking.detail: The tourist eVisa is not a work visa. A public appearance can also engage event licensing and content review even without a fee, so the host should not rely on payment as the boundary.
unpaid-speaking.next: Obtain the host's written visa and General Entertainment Authority or venue classification before accepting or announcing the talk.
unpaid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

paid-speaking.route: Temporary work visa and host contract
paid-speaking.detail: The temporary-work framework supports time-limited contracted work, requires a signed contract and medical insurance, and allows 90 days with a possible further 90 days. A resident payer must apply Saudi withholding tax to qualifying payments to a non-resident at the applicable rate.
paid-speaking.next: Have the Saudi contracting entity arrange the temporary-work visa, confirm the exact tax category and put fees, flights, hotels and other benefits in the contract.
paid-speaking.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

book-launch.route: Host-led work or event route plus licensed Saudi publisher, bookseller and publication review
book-launch.detail: Rights and publisher meetings can use the commercial-visit lane. A reading, launch, promotion or sale is active activity; written publications and imports sit under Saudi publishing rules and local distribution controls.
book-launch.next: Use a Saudi publisher or bookseller to clear the title, handle imports and sales, and coordinate the author appearance and venue approval.
book-launch.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

ai-teaching.route: Temporary work visa or continuing employment route through the Saudi host
ai-teaching.detail: A guest workshop, institutional training or paid lecture is contracted delivery, not tourist activity. The host must also identify any education, professional or event approval for the actual venue and audience.
ai-teaching.next: Have the university, company or public body specify the teaching format, contract, duration and regulator, then sponsor the correct work route.
ai-teaching.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

remote-work.route: No dedicated Saudi digital-nomad route identified
remote-work.detail: The reviewed tourist eVisa expressly says it is not a work visa. No official visitor permission for routine foreign remote work was identified in this review.
remote-work.next: Do not use the tourist eVisa as a remote-work permission. Obtain a Saudi residence or work route, or written official advice for the exact facts.
remote-work.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

entrepreneur.route: MISA investment registration and company licensing, with Entrepreneur Residency where eligible
entrepreneur.detail: A foreign investor must register with the Ministry of Investment before investment activity, then obtain commercial registration and sector licences. The Premium Residency entrepreneur product has separate investment-round, ownership and approved-entity evidence; its higher tier links permanent status to substantial investment and Saudi job creation.
entrepreneur.next: Use the first visit for meetings, obtain incubator or investment support, then map MISA registration, commercial registration, activity licences and Entrepreneur Residency as separate gates.
entrepreneur.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

trade.route: Commercial visit for negotiations; registered and licensed operation for local delivery
trade.detail: Supplier meetings, negotiations and market exploration can use a Saudi-hosted commercial visit. Installation, demonstrations, local selling and contracted services can require temporary work and a licensed Saudi counterparty. ATA Carnet pre-approval is available for eligible temporary goods.
trade.next: Appoint a Saudi importer, distributor or event contractor and pre-clear professional equipment or exhibition goods through ZATCA.
trade.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

artist.route: Temporary work visa plus promoter and entertainment licences
artist.detail: Live performance and entertainment events require the Saudi promoter to use the General Entertainment Authority licensing framework. Artist, support staff, venue, program and content details can all matter.
artist.next: Contract through a licensed promoter that confirms temporary-work visas, performance and event licences, content approval, withholding tax and merchandise.
artist.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

mixed-mission.route: Commercial or event visit for passive components plus temporary work and sector approvals for delivery
mixed-mission.detail: Meetings, a UNESCO forum, private training, a public keynote, book activity and performance can require different permissions on one itinerary. The tourist eVisa cannot be stretched across the active lines.
mixed-mission.next: Give one Saudi host or local coordinator a line-by-line activity, payer, venue and content matrix and obtain the invitation, visa and licence for each component.
mixed-mission.basis: From Luke's earlier notes; not yet verified against an official source.

filming.route: Ministry of Culture and Information authorisation
filming.detail: Smartraveller: producing or distributing printed or electronic material without the Ministry's authorisation is illegal.
filming.next: Ask the Saudi Embassy and the Ministry before filming.

research.route: Study or research visa with an accredited Saudi host
research.detail: Long-term study, work or research visas need acceptance from an accredited Saudi institution. There is no general visiting-researcher visa without a host.

laws.rule: Possession of illicit drugs and alcohol is illegal. Penalties are severe. Convictions for possession and trafficking of drugs may result in heavy fines, lengthy jail sentences, deportation or the death penalty. If you're in the company of someone who is involved in drug cases, including trafficking, possessing or using drugs, you may be detained and remain in detention until investigations of all parties are concluded. It is illegal to bring alcohol into Saudi Arabia and to possess or consume it in the country. Public intoxication or driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol is punishable by fines, imprisonment, deportation and confiscation of your driving licence.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: There are significant differences in the commercial, civil, family and employment laws between Australia and Saudi Arabia. If you're involved in local legal matters: seek professional legal advice understand your rights and what you must do under Saudi law. We can't interfere in commercial and family disputes. If you become involved in a commercial or employment dispute, your sponsor or employer may prevent you from leaving the country until the dispute is resolved. Commercial or labour dispute cases may take years to resolve. laws.heading: Commercial, civil, family and employment law

laws.rule: If you wish to marry a Saudi national, your partner will first need a letter of approval from the Ministry of Interior. Check current requirements and timeframes directly with the relevant local authorities.
laws.heading: Marriage

laws.rule: If you're a resident, you must always carry your resident identity card (Iqama). If you travel on a visa, you should always carry your passport. Saudi authorities have the right to check ID. There are security checkpoints, both in cities and on roads between cities.
laws.heading: Resident identity card

laws.rule: It's illegal to: Insult, criticise, provoke, or question public order, religious values or public morals or act in a way that is offensive toward the royal family government leadership or Islam. Saudi authorities can detain you without charges if you're suspected of committing an offence and keep you detained while they investigate. not comply with police instructions. support any group or organisation considered by Saudi authorities to practice violence. These actions are also illegal in social media posts, even if they were made outside Saudi Arabia and years prior to your visit. Foreigners have received lengthy prison sentences for offensive tweets made in the past. You may have to wait m
laws.heading: Serious offences

laws.rule: It's illegal to import, possess or trade in weapons and items held to be 'contrary to the beliefs of Islam'.
laws.heading: Illegal items

laws.rule: In Saudi Arabia, it's illegal to: preach or publicly practice a religion other than Islam produce or distribute printed or electronic material, without the Ministry of Culture and Information's authorisation publicly display or wear non-Islamic religious symbols or text that has symbols or slogans that could be viewed as political or clothes with profane language or image carrying flags or banners, especially when performing Hajj and Umrah be involved in charity and fundraising activities, including online or via social media without prior approval from local authorities post advertisements that result in an income on social media without a licence from the relevant local Saudi authorities.
laws.heading: Other illegal activities

laws.rule: Same-sex relationships and impersonating the opposite sex are illegal. Saudi Arabia doesn't recognise or allow same-sex marriages and rights. Authorities can impose fines and severe punishment, including deportation.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ laws

laws.rule: You will not be able to enter Saudi Arabia if your passport shows 'X' in the gender field.
laws.heading: Passports with 'X' gender identifier

laws.rule: The Islamic holy month of Ramadan is strictly observed in Saudi Arabia. Take care not to offend others and cultural customs during this time. It is illegal to eat, drink or smoke in public between sunrise and sunset during Ramadan. Authorities can detain and even deport you for doing so. Explore our Ramadan page to learn more, including dates for Ramadan.
laws.heading: Ramadan

laws.rule: Segregation in public places is now less strict than in previous years, particularly in major urban centres. However, some facilities, including the Riyadh Metro, gyms, pools, restaurants and shops, may continue to designate areas by gender or families.
laws.heading: Segregation

laws.rule: Individual travellers seeking to share accommodation have sometimes been refused joint occupancy. The situation is changing as the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia transforms. You should contact your accommodation provider to seek clarification on the requirements. It is important to respect local customs and act in a culturally appropriate manner. Further information can be found on the Visit Saudi Official Website.
laws.heading: Accommodation

laws.rule: Saudi Arabia has strict codes of behaviour. You can be fined for violating Saudi Arabia's Public Decency Regulations. Locals may be offended if you don't respect these codes. They may interpret this as religious or cultural disrespect.
laws.heading: Behaviour

laws.rule: Get advice on what is acceptable clothing before you arrive. Both men and women are asked to dress modestly in public in line with Public Decency Laws. Avoid tight fitting clothing or clothes with profane language or images. Men and women visiting Saudi Arabia should cover their shoulders and knees in public. If you don’t comply with these requirements, you may face penalties. If approached by authorities, be respectful and remain calm.
laws.heading: Dress

laws.rule: Before you travel: check if your medication is a controlled substance by visiting the Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) website. some medications require a permit, for information check the SFDA Permit Guidelines. Failure to obtain a permit may result in arrest and prosecution. Saudi authorities may detain or deport travellers for: carrying medication to treat HIV/AIDS or hepatitis testing positive for HIV/AIDS or hepatitis.
laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: Saudi Arabia has strict requirements for driver’s licences. If you’re a resident in Saudi Arabia, you'll need to get a Saudi driver’s licence. To drive in Saudi Arabia, you'll need: a valid Australian driver's licence (digital driver's licences may not be accepted) an International Driving Permit (IDP) You must get your IDP before departing Australia. Visitors to Saudi Arabia can only drive hire cars and not privately owned vehicles. You may only be allowed to use your Australian driving licence
laws.heading: Driving permit

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Saudi Arabian Riyal (SAR). If you are carrying currency, financial instruments, gold, precious metals, gemstones or jewellery with a total value of more than SAR40,000 or equivalent per family or group, you must declare these items on arrival or departure, including at land, sea or air border crossings. This applies to all forms of currency, not only cash. You can exchange currency at commercial banks and exchange bureaux. ATMs are widely available throughout Saudi Arabia. Check with your bank if your cards will work in Saudi Arabia.

visa-preparation.entry_summary: Smartraveller advises Do not travel and to postpone planned travel, including for religious pilgrimage. A valid visa is needed: Australia is on the list of countries eligible for the tourist eVisa from the official Visit Saudi portal. Other purposes need a separate visa through agencies accredited to the Saudi Embassy.
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Tourist eVisa online: one year, multiple entry, stays of up to 90 days.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Apply only on visa.visitsaudi.com (beware fraudulent links), match the visa to the purpose, and check for any past travel ban or unresolved legal case. Hajj visas go only through the Nusuk platform.
visa-preparation.useful_stay: Tourist eVisa valid 12 months, multiple entry, up to 90 days in total during that time; it can't be extended or used for any work.

steps.step: Apply and pay for the tourist eVisa on the official portal.
For any purpose other than tourism, get the matching visa through an agency accredited to the Saudi Embassy.
If transiting, check whether a transit visa is needed.
Check visa annotations: a business or visit visa marked 'via air' may not allow land entry.
Hajj and Umrah pilgrims register through Nusuk, the only approved platform for Hajj visas.

documents: Tourist eVisa (or the visa matching the purpose)
Guardian travelling with any tourist under 18
Yellow fever certificate if arriving from a risk area
Polio vaccination proof for under-15s from polio outbreak countries
open_questions: Is the tourist eVisa being used for an activity that Saudi Arabia treats as work or professional delivery?
Has the Saudi entity issued the invitation, or is there only a conference registration receipt?
Is unpaid participation being assumed to be outside event and work regulation?
Does the contract match the authorised host, role, location and temporary-work period?
Has the promoter obtained the required entertainment, venue and content licences before publicity?
Are books, equipment, merchandise or exhibition goods approved for import or temporary admission?
Has the Saudi payer classified and budgeted withholding tax on the non-resident payment?
Does the founder plan include MISA registration, commercial registration and sector licensing rather than residence alone?
What does the tourist eVisa cost today, including any insurance? The portal's home page doesn't show the amount.
